exposure: transvaginal ultrasonography measurement of cervical length
cohort: 126 pregnant women at 37-40 weeks of gestation with a singleton foetus undergoing labour induction.
finding: A Bishop score >= 3 and cervical length <= 2.5 cm were significantly associated with vaginal delivery and shorter induction-to-delivery time, demonstrating similar predictive accuracy for successful labour induction.
mod_finding: A Bishop score >= 3 and cervical length <= 2.5 cm were significantly associated with vaginal delivery and a lower caesarean section rate.
